### Mephibosheth Sits at the King’s Table
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/mephibosheth-sits-at-kings-table
Passage: 2 Samuel 9:13
Points:
- David actively remembered and fulfilled his covenant commitment to Jonathan even after reaching supreme royal power.
- Biblical kindness (*hesed*) is steadfast covenant love that expresses itself through tangible, sacrificial action.
- Mephibosheth was from the family of David's enemy, yet he was granted royal restoration and daily provision.
- David's gracious treatment of Mephibosheth points forward to Jesus dying to save His enemies.
- Followers of Christ are called to show compassionate love to the vulnerable who cannot repay them.

### Receiving the Unmerited Favor of God
Author: Michael Youssef, Ph.D.
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-week-of-september-2-2024.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 9:3
Points:
- Rather than pursuing retribution against Saul's household, David eagerly searched for someone to whom he could show mercy.
- Mephibosheth's lameness and exile in Lo Debar symbolize humanity's helpless condition before God.
- David restored ancestral property to Mephibosheth and welcomed him to eat at his table as family.
- God extends unmerited grace to sinners through Jesus Christ, just as David blessed Mephibosheth for Jonathan's sake.
- Understanding God's free grace compels believers to extend kindness and mercy to those around them.

### Have Mercy
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/greg-laurie-devotion-march-17-2025.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 9:8
Points:
- Ancient monarchs usually eliminated rivals, but King David chose radical generosity toward Saul's grandson.
- David honored his past promise to Jonathan by elevating Mephibosheth to eat like one of the king's own sons.
- Mephibosheth's sense of unworthiness mirrors humanity's complete inability to earn God's favor.
- God actively seeks out lost and fearful sinners to adopt them into His royal family.
- God offers grace freely, but individuals must take the step of faith to accept His royal invitation.

### Bible Pathway - April 13
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-april-13-2013.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 9:7
Points:
- David prioritized honoring his lifelong covenant of brotherhood with Jonathan above personal comfort or suspicion.
- Returning Saul's royal estate to Mephibosheth demonstrated that doing what is right in God's eyes transcends material cost.
- True relational healing requires intentional effort to overcome fear and pride.
- Experiencing God's abundant forgiveness calls believers to extend generous forgiveness to others.
- Spiritual maturity involves humbling oneself and taking initiative to restore broken relationships.
